summary: Generates static, sample-indexed channel patterns such as ramps, waves, random values, lookup tables, SOP-ready curves, and instancing arrays.
key_concepts: Pattern CHOP generates a sequence of samples in a channel with no reference to time in seconds or frames.
It is useful for lookup tables, simple curves that can become SOP data, and instance attributes for Geometry COMP workflows.
All defaults are in samples; the operator has Length in samples rather than a start/end time range.
An optional input CHOP can provide length and sample-rate matching while Combine Channels decides append, insert, replace, add, or multiply behavior.
One cycle spans the full channel length by default no matter how many samples are generated.
Use Wave CHOP or LFO CHOP for time-driven oscillation instead of Pattern CHOP's static sample-indexed arrays.

key_params.name: wavetype
key_params.note: Constant, sine, cosine, triangle, ramp, square, pulse, random, step, and other pattern types

key_params.name: numcycles
key_params.note: Number of cycles over the channel length

key_params.name: combine
key_params.note: Append, insert, replace, add, or multiply generated channels with input

key_params.name: append
key_params.note: Append generated channels after input channels

key_params.name: insert
key_params.note: Insert generated channels before input channels

key_params.name: replace
key_params.note: Replace input channels by channel-name matching

key_params.name: add
key_params.note: Add generated and input channels by channel-name matching

key_params.name: multiply
key_params.note: Multiply generated and input channels by channel-name matching

key_params.name: autoexportroot
key_params.note: Root path for automatic channel-name exports

key_params.name: exporttable
key_params.note: DAT table used by DAT table export methods

common_gotchas: Pattern CHOP is sample-indexed and non-time-based; use Wave CHOP/LFO CHOP for timeline/time-driven oscillation.
Defaults are in samples, not seconds or frames, though the output still carries a sample rate.
There is no start/end range, only length in samples.
Optional input can provide length/sample-rate matching and can be combined by append/insert/replace/add/multiply modes.
One cycle spans the whole channel length by default regardless of sample count.
Use me.chanIndex expressions for per-generated-channel parameter customization.
